note: Lead's question on the cut card: read alone, it still presents both sides fairly. Kennedy's call is scoped to NEW vaccines and the re-testing of vaccines in use is attributed to Benn and Kulldorff, so dropping his 'not suggesting we go back' remark misattributes nothing; the case against dummy shots keeps its reason through Black's Prevnar sentence (the control babies got a shot with a possible benefit), so Offit's 'unethical' is not reasonless. No add-back required. If room is ever made, Salmon's point is the cleanest steel-man: 'Daniel Salmon of Johns Hopkins argues that where a vaccine already exists, a new one cannot ethically be tested against none.'
